Scenario
As part of final readiness, you must complete an integrated practical inspection under mock assessment
conditions. You will inspect, record evidence, explain findings and identify any further work or authorisation
needed.
Objectives
• Demonstrate safe independent working under mock conditions.
• Carry out an integrated vehicle inspection methodically.
• Record findings, measurements and recommendations clearly.
• Explain decisions using evidence and correct terminology.
• Reflect on readiness for EPA-style practical assessment.

• Inspection checklist and job card

• Manufacturer technical information

TASK 4: BASIC BRAKE AND TYRE
CONDITION CHECK
Autocare Technician Level 2 | Block 1 | v2.1
TIME
60 minutes
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge | Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT
Weeks 1-10
Your task
A vehicle has been reported with possible tyre and brake wear during a basic workshop check. You must inspect
visible brake and tyre components, record measurements and explain any customer recommendations.
What you must do
1
Prepare the vehicle and work area safely.
2
Inspect tyre condition, tread depth, pressure and visible damage.
3
Inspect visible brake components and record condition.
4
Record wheel torque setting and any relevant technical data.
5
Explain findings to the assessor/workplace mentor and reinstate the workstation.
What good evidence looks like
SAFE SETUP
Suitable PPE, a prepared work area and controlled vehicle or
equipment.
CORRECT METHOD
A logical sequence using the relevant procedure and technical
information.
ACCURATE EVIDENCE
Actual readings, findings and actions recorded clearly and
precisely.
SOUND DECISIONS
Appropriate recommendations, referral or authorisation
supported by evidence.
You will need
• Light vehicle
• Tread depth gauge and tyre pressure gauge
• Wheel brace/torque wrench
• Brake inspection tools
• Manufacturer technical information
• Apprentice Assessment Record

charging system checks, record results and explain whether further work is required.

• Take relevant electrical measurements using a multimeter or tester.

TASK 3: INTERIM SERVICE, INSPECTION AND
DOCUMENTATION
Autocare Technician Level 2 | Block 3 | v2.1
TIME
60 minutes
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge | Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT
Weeks 21-30
Your task
A vehicle is booked for an interim service. You must follow the service schedule, identify required service items,
complete the inspection documentation and record any additional work requiring customer authorisation.
What you must do
1
Prepare the vehicle and workstation safely.
2
Identify required service items and technical information.
3
Carry out service checks as instructed by the assessor/workplace mentor.
4
Record findings, parts required and any additional work.
5
Reinstate the vehicle and workstation and complete documentation.
What good evidence looks like
SAFE SETUP
Suitable PPE, a prepared work area and controlled vehicle or
equipment.
CORRECT METHOD
A logical sequence using the relevant procedure and technical
information.
ACCURATE EVIDENCE
Actual readings, findings and actions recorded clearly and
precisely.
SOUND DECISIONS
Appropriate recommendations, referral or authorisation
supported by evidence.
You will need
• Light vehicle
• Service schedule
• Oil filter/air filter examples where required
• Fluid measuring/checking equipment
• Proforma/job card documentation
• PPE and Apprentice Assessment Record

Block_3_Task_4_Environmental_Spill_and_W.instructions:
TASK 4: ENVIRONMENTAL SPILL RESPONSE
AND WASTE CONTROL
Autocare Technician Level 2 | Block 3 | v2.1
TIME
45 minutes
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge | Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT
Weeks 21-30
Your task
During routine workshop activity, a fluid spill and several waste items are identified. You must make the area
safe, identify waste streams, record the incident and explain how environmental controls prevent harm.
What you must do
1
Assess the work area and identify immediate risks.
2
Select PPE and control the spill or simulated spill as instructed.
3
Identify correct waste stream controls for fluids and contaminated materials.
4
Complete an incident or environmental record.
5
Explain corrective actions and reinstate the work area.
What good evidence looks like
SAFE SETUP
Suitable PPE, a prepared work area and controlled vehicle or
equipment.
CORRECT METHOD
A logical sequence using the relevant procedure and technical
information.
ACCURATE EVIDENCE
Actual readings, findings and actions recorded clearly and
precisely.
SOUND DECISIONS
Appropriate recommendations, referral or authorisation
supported by evidence.
You will need
• Workshop area or simulated spill scenario
• Spill kit and signage
• COSHH information or safety data sheets
• Waste stream labels/containers
• PPE and Apprentice Assessment Record

Autocare Technician Level 2 | Block 8 | v2.1
TIME
60 minutes
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge | Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT

Your task
A vehicle has excessive or uneven tyre wear. You must inspect the tyres and related steering/suspension
geometry, record evidence and identify the likely root cause before recommending work.
What you must do
1
Prepare the vehicle and complete tyre/alignment pre-checks.
2
Record tyre wear patterns and pressures.
3
Measure or interpret alignment/geometry data as instructed.
4
Identify likely root cause and recommended action.
5
Record findings and reinstate the workstation.

equipment.

A logical sequence using the relevant procedure and technical
information.

precisely.

supported by evidence.

Block_9_Task_4_ADAS_Pre_Calibration_Chec.instructions:
TASK 4: ADAS PRE-CALIBRATION AND
SENSOR AWARENESS CHECK
Autocare Technician Level 2 | Block 9 | v2.1
TIME
60 minutes
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge | Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT
Weeks 81-94
Your task
A vehicle has had alignment, tyre or body-related work and may require ADAS checks. You must complete
non-invasive pre-calibration checks, record findings and identify whether specialist calibration referral is required.
What you must do
1
Prepare the vehicle and identify visible ADAS features.
2
Carry out pre-checks for tyres, ride height, alignment and visible sensor damage.
3
Record findings and compare with available guidance.
4
Decide whether the vehicle is suitable for calibration or requires correction/referral.
5
Explain the outcome to the assessor/workplace mentor and complete documentation.
What good evidence looks like
SAFE SETUP
Suitable PPE, a prepared work area and controlled vehicle or
equipment.
CORRECT METHOD
A logical sequence using the relevant procedure and technical
information.
ACCURATE EVIDENCE
Actual readings, findings and actions recorded clearly and
precisely.
SOUND DECISIONS
Appropriate recommendations, referral or authorisation
supported by evidence.
You will need
• Light vehicle or ADAS case-study pack
• Manufacturer guidance or sample calibration report
• Tyre pressure gauge/alignment data where available
• PPE and Apprentice Assessment Record
